level1.text: The average power of a wind turbine over a week ($168\,\text{h}$) is $2.5\,\text{MW}$. How much electricity does it produce in a week? Give the answer in megawatt-hours.

A hydropower plant runs for $8.0\,\text{h}$ at a power of $120\,\text{MW}$ when the consumption of electricity is high in the evening. How much energy does the plant produce during this time? Give the answer in megawatt-hours.
The power of the Olkiluoto 3 nuclear power plant is $1.6\,\text{GW}$. How much energy does the plant produce in a day when it runs at this power all the time? Give the answer in gigawatt-hours.

In 2024 Finland produced a total of $79.9\,\text{TWh}$ of electricity, and the share of wind power was $20.2\,\text{TWh}$ (Statistics Finland). What percentage of the electricity was produced by wind power?

The power of the solar panels of a detached house in the middle of a summer day is $4.0\,\text{kW}$. How much electricity do the panels produce in $3.5\,\text{h}$, when the power stays the same? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

level2.text: The wind farm in the example has a rated power of $25\,\text{MW}$, and its average power over the year is $32\,\%$ of the rated power. How much electricity does the farm produce in a year, when a year has $8760\,\text{h}$? Give the answer in gigawatt-hours.

Finnish hydropower produced about $14\,\text{TWh}$ of electricity in 2024 (Statistics Finland). For how many hours would Olkiluoto 3 ($1.6\,\text{GW}$) have to run at full power to produce the same energy? Give the answer in hours.

Nuclear power plants produced about $31\,\text{TWh}$ of electricity in 2024. The wind turbine in the example produces $12\,\text{GWh}$ in a year. How many such wind turbines would be needed to produce the same annual energy as the nuclear power plants produced?

Olkiluoto 3 ($1.6\,\text{GW}$) runs at full power for the whole year ($8760\,\text{h}$). A household without electric heating in the example uses $5000\,\text{kWh}$ in a year. How many households' annual consumption would the plant cover? Give the answer in millions of households.

level3.text: The frosty evening in the example: the consumption of electricity in Finland is $11\,\text{GW}$. Nuclear power plants run at a power of $3.5\,\text{GW}$. The combined rated power of wind turbines is $9.0\,\text{GW}$, but the wind is weak and they produce only $4.0\,\%$ of their rated power. How much power must other power plants and imported electricity produce? Give the answer in gigawatts.

The wind farm and the nuclear power plant in the example have the same rated power, $600\,\text{MW}$. The average power of the wind farm is $33\,\%$ and that of the nuclear power plant $90\,\%$ of the rated power. How many times as much energy does the nuclear power plant produce in a year? Give the answer as a factor.

The municipality in the example proposes a solar park that would replace Olkiluoto 3 ($1600\,\text{MW}$). The average power of the solar park over the year is $11\,\%$ and that of Olkiluoto 3 $90\,\%$ of the rated power. How large should the rated power of the solar park be for it to produce as much energy in a year as Olkiluoto 3? Give the answer in gigawatts. Also consider whether such a park would replace Olkiluoto 3 on a January evening.
